Addressed the Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Amendment Bill, said the coalition would not block its passage despite calling it duplicative and politically motivated with fines of $1 million or more for breaches, and quoted industry groups including the Minerals Council warning it would add delay without environmental benefit.

Supported the Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Amendment Bill, described his Ipswich electorate's coal mining history, and said the government's $150 million commitment established an independent expert scientific committee on coal seam gas and coal mining impacts on water resources.

Supported the EPBC bill as filling a gap where the assessment process could not consider water impacts, described the Hunter Estuary Wetlands, an internationally recognised Ramsar site covering almost 3,000 hectares near a coal seam gas exploration well, and said 1,500 protesters had rallied in Newcastle against expanded coal loading infrastructure.

Criticised the government for introducing the EPBC amendment 10 months after he first raised water concerns, saying it came too late for the Gloucester region where gas wells had already been approved, and said the minister should apologise to residents who trusted the member for Lyne's advocacy on the issue.

Supported the EPBC amendment bill as the first time the federal government could assess coal seam gas and large coal mine impacts on water resources, cited a Lismore referendum in which 88 per cent of 15,000 voters opposed coal seam gas exploration in the council area, and said thousands had marched against coal seam gas in Lismore and Murwillumbah.

Opposed the Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Amendment Bill 2013 as a political move that will not resolve coal seam gas access and compensation issues, noted the National Farmers' Federation called the bill inadequate, and recounted visiting coal seam gas areas in Roma and the Darling Downs.

Supported the Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Amendment Bill 2013 as protection for water resources and prime agricultural land in the Northern Rivers, cited National Water Commission and CSIRO findings on coal seam gas risks to water, and noted the National Farmers' Federation wants stronger regulation rather than opposing the bill.

Supported the intent of the Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Amendment Bill 2013 but warned it could delay coal seam gas well approvals needed for Gladstone LNG export projects worth $77 billion and employing 30,000 people.

Said he takes an agnostic position on coal seam gas, wanting both environmental safeguards and the jobs the industry can bring to regional communities, noted its emissions are about 70 per cent lower than coal, and accused Labor members of only recently discovering an issue regional communities have discussed for years.

Argued that the bill would make water resources a matter of national environmental significance for coal seam gas and large coalmining developments, enabling national assessment of their impacts while supporting environmentally sustainable industry and protection of water resources.

Supported the bill, arguing that independent scientific advice and harmonised regulatory frameworks would promote best practice in coal seam gas and coalmining, allow environmentally compliant projects to proceed, support regional jobs and help address a potential gas shortage.

The speaker moved to call on the Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Amendment Bill 2013 immediately and give it precedence over all other business until 4:30 pm that day; the motion was agreed to.

The senator supported the Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Amendment Bill 2013 to protect aquifers from coal mining and coal seam gas, and criticised Tony Windsor for selling his farm to a coal miner at $5,000 per acre while opposing nearby mines.
